statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2
s has exactly n minus 1 entries
each entry of s is either plus 1 or minus 1
a is a permutation of the set {1, 2, ..., n}, so each integer from 1 to n appears exactly once
the inequality at each position is strict: si times (a(i+1) minus a(i)) must be positive
the condition is imposed for every i from 1 to n minus 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, among all sign sequences of length n minus 1 with entries plus or minus 1, characterize exactly those sequences that maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose successive differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: Fix an integer n with n at least 2
Consider all sign sequences s of length n minus 1 with each entry plus or minus 1
For each such s, count all permutations a of 1 through n satisfying the adjacency inequalities for every index i from 1 to n minus 1
For each n, identify exactly those sign sequences s for which this count is maximal among all admissible sign sequences of that length

variables.name: s
i

variables.domain: all orderings of the integers from 1 to n

witness_dependencies: The permutations counted by f(s) depend on both n and s
The maximizing sign sequence is allowed to depend on n
The statement asks for all maximizers, so there may be more than one maximizing sequence for a given n
